name: old rusty diesel generator box seen from above: vented top with fuel cap and exhaust pipe, front control panel with dials, cables on the ground
label: wasteland_ruins/generator

surfaces.part: front control panel face with dials

answer.evidence: The main body has a green vented top at rows 5-17 (13 rows), with slots and a fuel cap seen from above. A dark front-edge line at row 18 is followed by eave shadow at rows 19-20. Below it, rows 19-30 are the front face with the control panel, dials and a yellow gauge. The exhaust pipe rises above the top at rows 1-11 and has a small rounded cap at rows 1-4. The cables on the ground sit at the bottom rows. The top and front face are both clearly drawn, so it reads as a 3/4 view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is small, about 20x20 source pixels, so I judged it mostly on the measured facts plus what is visible at that size. It has 16 visible tones per tile, level with the cheese stall (17) and the well (20) and above the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 4%, below the stall's 13%. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans green-grey and follows the adjacent material rather than forming a black sticker line. The body, vented top and control panel show roughly 4 lightness steps with speckle, dials and rust variation, slightly fewer than the references' 5-6. It does not look thinner or flatter than the stall or well beside it, so I rate it equal on density and passing.

The exhaust pipe at rows 1-11 is a small vertical stack on top, and it does not change the reading of the main body as a box with a visible top and front.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts favour the candidate. It has 16 visible tones per tile against 17 for stall-cheese, 20 for well-roofed and 9 for hedge. Near-flat coverage is 4%, well under stall-cheese at 13%. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans dark green or dark rust beside the body and is not a sticker line. By eye, the green casing has about 4 lightness steps, and the vented top, fuel cap, exhaust pipe, panel dials and ground cables break up the surface with dots and variation. It has no large flat fills. It is a little thinner than the best references, with only 23 distinct colours in total against 38-40 for the richer ones, and its ramps are about 4 steps against 5-6. A careful artist would still accept it beside the stall and well.
